objective: Build a practical Unreal-native AIGC production Agent that turns current scene intent into real image, PBR, Blender-generated geometry, asset, PCG and lighting work, coordinates these capabilities through a hand-built durable typed runtime, and returns editable results through isolated Unreal candidates without accumulating approval gates, audit subsystems or decorative framework layers.

milestones.title: Real Comfy baseline and contract-first seams
milestones.outcome: The real RTX 4080 baseline remains reproducible and scene, provider, route, approval and receipt boundaries validate across Python, TypeScript and Unreal C++.
acceptance: Real baseline and cross-language contract evidence are recorded without overstating human adoption

milestones.title: Hand-built Agent kernel and scene context
milestones.outcome: A verified Scene Package becomes durable AgentRun context in an append-only SQLite event model reconstructed by a deterministic reducer and exposed through a bounded capability registry.
acceptance: Restart reconstructs the same state and pending interrupt from events
Scene attachment and tool side effects are idempotent
The model cannot mutate authoritative state or bypass typed policy

milestones.title: Scene Lab and typed Agent event UI
milestones.outcome: A redesigned visual-production workspace exposes scene constraints, Agent lifecycle, tool actions, persisted approvals, recovery and evidence through typed streaming state.
acceptance: Refresh preserves the current run and pending decision, and every visible proof maps to real state or evidence

milestones.title: Real Unreal scene and matched provider routing
milestones.outcome: One real Unreal scene package runs through local ComfyUI and Codex built-in GPT Image 2 using the same constraints and normalized receipts without a permission prompt.
acceptance: Both real execution surfaces are bound to the same verified scene intent, persist normalized receipts, recover idempotently and remain explicitly unselected

milestones.title: Evaluation tribunal and bounded revision
milestones.outcome: Independent deterministic and multimodal evaluators expose disagreement, reject attractive-invalid candidates and verify one evidence-selected mask-bounded revision.
acceptance: An attractive negative control is rejected and evaluator evidence replays without regenerating images

milestones.title: Recovery observability memory and evaluation
milestones.outcome: The Agent survives injected failures without duplicate side effects, emits correlated OpenTelemetry evidence, governs production memory and reports frozen Harness evaluations.
acceptance: Recovery, context, policy and memory scorecards report denominators, latency and cost from reproducible cases

milestones.title: Verified provenance and portfolio case study
milestones.outcome: The complete Unreal-to-provider-to-tribunal-to-adoption-to-reimport story ships with independently verified C2PA provenance and inspectable evidence for every public claim.
acceptance: One successful run and one failure-injected run can be independently replayed and verified

milestones.title: Scene Digital Twin and staged Scene Delta kernel
milestones.outcome: A real UE 5.8 scene exports stable 3D facts and accepts a frozen typed lighting/PCG SceneChangePlan whose dry-run proves dependency, scope, fingerprint, deterministic seed, validation and cleanup semantics before any host mutation.
acceptance: The extended scene package records actor, material, light, PCG, data-layer, bounds and protected-object facts with content hashes
A discriminated SceneChangePlan supports bounded lighting and PCG operations, rejects arbitrary code and validates as a dependency DAG
A real UE dry-run receipt resolves staging strategy and write scope without modifying the source level

milestones.title: ComfyUI production graph and PBR material route
milestones.outcome: Reviewed ComfyUI subgraphs and verified production nodes compile visual intent into validated PBR texture sets and Unreal material instances without arbitrary graph execution.
acceptance: Runtime capability inspection proves every required custom node and workflow version
One real PBR set passes channel, size, hash and material-instance validation in UE

milestones.title: PCG lighting and asset scene-transformation closed loop
milestones.outcome: One project-owned concept target drives staged lighting, PCG layout and bounded asset/material changes, same-camera rerender evaluation, failed-domain correction and verified publish or discard.
acceptance: The source camera, protected actors and walkable bounds remain invariant while the staged 3D scene visibly changes
Technical and visual evaluators produce independent evidence and correction reruns only the failed branch
The real UE result is published or discarded from a replayable receipt with no duplicate side effect

milestones.title: MCP interoperability image-to-3D experiment and portfolio release
milestones.outcome: A thin MCP facade exposes the same bounded resources and tools, one optional image-to-3D provider passes through Interchange validation, and a Chinese screenshot-rich case study truthfully demonstrates the complete Unreal scene-transformation Agent.
acceptance: MCP calls enter the existing policy, event, idempotency and validation path and expose no arbitrary host execution
One generated GLB candidate is either admitted or rejected by recorded license, geometry, material, collision and budget checks while the main route still works without it
The public release distinguishes implemented, experimental and planned capabilities and maps every claim to host evidence

milestones.title: Live Scene Session and Scene Change Spectrum
milestones.outcome: A real imported Unreal scene opens an interactive Scene Session where the user states a visual intent, scopes bounded image, material, asset, PCG and lighting domains, and inspects a deterministic typed Scene Delta draft through ArtFlow's distinctive Scene Change Spectrum interface.
acceptance: Scene Session planning derives only from the attached scene, registered capabilities and explicit user scope and causes no external side effect
The interface communicates domain readiness, dependencies and guarded boundaries without resembling a chat shell, arbitrary node graph or generic AI dashboard
A staged execution request can be content-bound to the draft and current scene without granting arbitrary host execution

milestones.title: Unreal editor session bridge and candidate execution
milestones.outcome: The Unreal editor can initiate a Scene Session, receive a typed candidate-stage request and execute registered scene tools in an isolated candidate level with durable receipts and reconciliation.
acceptance: One editor-originated session completes inspect, draft, stage, rerender and reconcile against the project-owned UE 5.8 host
Retry and restart produce no duplicate asset, Actor or provider side effect

milestones.title: Cross-pipeline scene transformation and failed-domain correction
milestones.outcome: Reviewed ComfyUI graphs, GPT Image 2 development orchestration, PBR materials, project and generated assets, PCG and lighting cooperate through one typed plan, with independent evaluation and failed-domain-only correction.
acceptance: At least two materially different production cases use different capability routes while sharing the same coordinator and evidence model
A deliberately failed domain is corrected without rerunning successful branches

milestones.title: Embedded delivery and portfolio release
milestones.outcome: ArtFlow ships as a polished Chinese portfolio product with an Unreal-facing entry, multiple reproducible production cases, restrained documentation, real screenshots and a traceable release package.
acceptance: A reviewer can understand, launch and verify the core workflow without reading development history
Public claims and screenshots are generated from frozen host receipts and versioned cases

milestones.title: Evidence-bound disposition and versioned Unreal publish
milestones.outcome: The orchestrator adopts or rejects Session candidates from persisted evaluation evidence and publishes accepted work as a versioned Unreal scene variant with replayable provenance, without overwriting the source level or duplicating package side effects.
acceptance: A typed disposition decision can reference only an accepted domain evaluation and exact candidate content identity
Unreal publishes an accepted candidate only into a content-addressed ArtFlow Published namespace while the source level remains byte-identical
A lost publish receipt is reconciled by a fresh process without creating a second package, and rejected candidates cannot enter the published namespace

milestones.title: Scene Variant Ledger and embedded Unreal review
milestones.outcome: The Scene Change Spectrum presents evaluation, correction, adoption and versioned publish as one legible scene-variant lineage, while a registered Unreal review action opens the exact published map and returns a typed inspection receipt without exposing arbitrary paths or host execution.
acceptance: The Chinese product UI distinguishes candidate, corrected, adopted, published and reconciled states from real receipts rather than simulated progress
A reviewer can inspect the exact content-addressed published variant from the Unreal-facing entry while the source level remains untouched
Desktop and narrow screenshots demonstrate a recognizable scene-directing interface rather than a chat shell, node canvas or generic AI dashboard

milestones.title: Durable live scene-variant lifecycle
milestones.outcome: Evaluation, failed-domain correction, Codex adoption, Unreal publish and review become first-class append-only Scene Session events, so the live workspace projects the current run's real variant lifecycle instead of depending on frozen showcase data.
acceptance: Typed lifecycle events bind every evaluation, correction, adoption, publish and review transition to one Scene Session, stage request and candidate identity
Loopback Unreal receipts append exactly once and restart reconstructs the same current variant without a parallel state machine
The Scene Change Spectrum renders live projected lifecycle state for a real editor-originated Session while frozen showcase data remains an explicit demo fallback only

milestones.title: Unreal-native lifecycle callback
milestones.outcome: The Unreal-facing bridge appends registered evaluation, adoption, publish and review receipts directly to the matching current Scene Session, replacing the one-off historical migration route while preserving the same reducer and projection.
acceptance: Unreal can submit only registered content identities for the current run and Session and cannot supply a host path or arbitrary lifecycle schema
Each callback transition appends exactly once, rejects reordered or mismatched receipts, and projects immediately in the live Scene Change Spectrum
The M16 migration route is retained only as a reproducible compatibility fixture and is not the normal product path

milestones.title: Live candidate execution and progress
milestones.outcome: A staged Candidate Plan becomes a content-bound work item that the Unreal editor can claim, execute and reconcile from the current Scene Session, with typed progress returning through the existing event stream and no manual command-line launch.
acceptance: Only the current Session's registered staged plan can enter the Unreal work queue, and no caller can supply an arbitrary command, script, workflow or host path
One Unreal writer claims a work item atomically, reports typed execution progress and reconciles unknown completion without duplicate scene or provider side effects
The Scene Change Spectrum renders queued, claimed, executing, reconciled and failed states from the live AgentRunProjection

milestones.title: Current-session tribunal and failed-domain correction
milestones.outcome: The current Scene Session evaluates its own Unreal candidate rerender and 3D host receipt, classifies failed domains, preserves passed evidence, submits only a bounded correction plan and advances an accepted candidate toward adoption without loading historical M16 evaluation artifacts.
acceptance: Technical checks and the visual critic evaluate the exact current work outcome and cannot cite another Session, candidate or showcase artifact
A failed domain produces one content-bound correction work item while passed domain evidence remains byte-identical and is not re-executed
A passing reevaluation appends the current candidate evaluation through AgentEventStore and projects the decision basis in the Scene Change Spectrum

milestones.title: Current-session versioned publish and Unreal review
milestones.outcome: The exact current candidate adopted by Codex is published into a content-addressed Unreal variant namespace, reconciled without duplicate packages and opened through the registered review action while the source level remains byte-identical.
acceptance: Publish derives only from the current persisted adoption and exact candidate bytes and cannot accept a caller path or arbitrary package name
A fresh UE process reconciles the same published package and receipt without a second package or source-level write
The live Scene Change Spectrum projects adopted, published and reviewed as distinct current-session states

milestones.title: Unreal-native operator lifecycle controls
milestones.outcome: An artist can advance the current Scene Session from candidate execution through correction, publish and exact-version review from registered Unreal editor actions, while the Scene Change Spectrum reflects each durable state without command-line operation.
acceptance: Editor actions derive the only legal next lifecycle command from the current Agent projection and never accept an arbitrary script, path, map or event payload
Publish and review show clear Chinese in-editor progress and reconcile an unknown completion before any retry
One continuous recorded walkthrough starts from the project-owned scene and reaches the exact Published variant using only product-facing entrypoints

milestones.title: Blender DCC production bridge and Unreal return
milestones.outcome: Blender becomes a complete DCC execution surface for current Scene Sessions: bounded modeling and Geometry Nodes, ComfyUI-driven PBR assembly and baking, scene layout, lighting and later simulation caches return editable project-owned results to isolated Unreal candidates through one durable work lifecycle.
acceptance: The Agent derives a typed modeling specification from current scene scale, placement bounds and visual intent rather than emitting Blender code
A real Blender 5.2 process creates an editable blend source, embedded GLB and preview from a fixed versioned modeling capability
Unreal Interchange imports the generated model into a Session-derived candidate namespace and records the resulting StaticMesh identity
The first production route supports modular architectural props, followed by ComfyUI PBR assembly, Geometry Nodes layout, camera and lighting exchange behind the same contract

milestones.title: Scene-conditioned ComfyUI production route
milestones.outcome: ComfyUI becomes a scene-conditioned generation surface beneath the ArtFlow control plane: Unreal passes drive reviewed ControlNet, LoRA and Production Nodes capabilities whose typed outputs continue into Blender and isolated Unreal candidates.
acceptance: The Agent discovers the real local ComfyUI and Production Nodes capabilities from runtime facts rather than documentation claims
A typed request binds exact Unreal render-pass identities, registered conditioning modes, model identities and bounded generation parameters
A reviewed fixed workflow produces one real scene-conditioned image or material candidate without model-authored graphs
The output joins the current Scene Session lifecycle and has a declared Blender or Unreal consumer

milestones.title: DCC capability graph and live dispatch
milestones.outcome: Blender's modeling, UV/material/bake, Geometry Nodes, lighting and later cache operations combine with reviewed ComfyUI subgraphs and typed Unreal tools as one discoverable Scene Session capability graph whose real work is dispatched and observed through the existing durable product lifecycle.
acceptance: The capability graph reports real Blender, ComfyUI and Unreal readiness with versioned typed inputs instead of treating each host script as a separate demo
Scene-conditioned lookdev can be dispatched, claimed, reconciled and observed through the existing Scene DCC Worker lifecycle
At least one additional non-modeling Blender production capability reaches an editable artifact and isolated Unreal consumer through the same contract
The product UI explains the cross-DCC scene change without exposing arbitrary host code or a generic node editor

milestones.title: Surface authoring and bake round-trip
milestones.outcome: The current Scene Session can ask Blender for bounded UV and material-bake work derived from an accepted lookdev direction, then return reusable textures and an editable exchange asset to a new isolated Unreal candidate through the same durable capability lifecycle.
acceptance: A typed request binds the current lookdev blend, Session identity, registered object scope, UV method, atlas resolution and finite bake channels
Blender creates a named UV set, baked material textures, editable blend and exchange asset without model-authored host code
Minimum UV coverage, texture readability, material-slot and geometry budgets are checked before Unreal import
Unreal imports the baked result into a Session-derived candidate, binds its generated material and reconciles a repeated return without changing the source level

milestones.title: Live surface capability dispatch
milestones.outcome: The proven Blender UV and material-bake route becomes a registered current-session capability in the existing DCC work lifecycle and Scene Change Spectrum, so an artist can dispatch and inspect it without using development scripts.
acceptance: The existing Scene DCC Work definition admits the exact surface request, Blender receipt and Unreal return identities as a sixth finite capability
Queue, claim, execute, reconcile and replay use the existing append-only worker with no parallel scheduler or approval gate
The product UI presents Lookdev input, UV atlas, Blender surface result and Unreal candidate as one legible route backed by current-session artifacts

nextSlice.title: Dispatch surface bake through Scene DCC Worker
nextSlice.outcome: Register the frozen M26 Surface Bake as the sixth Scene DCC capability, execute it through the existing durable worker and present its current-session media route in Scene Change Spectrum.
nonGoals: Do not rerun Blender, Unreal, ComfyUI or an image provider
Do not add a new worker, queue, state machine, approval layer or generic DCC framework
Do not broaden the surface schema or start another production domain
acceptance: SceneDccWorkDefinition validates and binds the M26 request, Blender receipt, Unreal receipt and artifact hashes
The existing DCC Worker persists one idempotent surface work item through queue, claim, execute, reconcile and replay
Scene Change Spectrum shows the M26 input, UV atlas, Blender preview and Unreal candidate from real artifact URLs at desktop and narrow widths
stopConditions: Stop if the frozen M26 identities no longer validate
Stop if integrating the capability would require a second work lifecycle
Stop if project-owned changes overlap unknown user edits and cannot be preserved

sourceOfTruth: observable code, tests and current artifacts

evidenceCeiling: M0-M26 are complete. A content-bound current-session Surface Request selected 27 registered Blender objects and fixed smart-project UV, 1024px atlas and Base Color/Roughness bake parameters. Blender 5.2 produced ArtFlow_BakedUV, five verified artifacts, 2,818 vertices and 5,364 triangles. Unreal 5.8 imported one mesh, one material and two textures into Surface_B_9cbf7f1f20ab; the repeated return reconciled with zero duplicate side effects and the source level remained byte-identical. Product dispatch of this sixth capability is M27-S1 scope.
constraints: ArtFlow Agent remains the independent flagship portfolio product; the sibling Art Pipeline Skill has separate Git and goal state and is only a reusable capability layer

Project-owned DCC and engine fixtures, bounded local GPU runs, built-in Codex image generation, candidate selection and local portfolio delivery are autonomous development scope; unrelated user data and shared installations remain protected
No arbitrary model-generated ComfyUI graph, Python, Shell or host-script execution
No deterministic failure may be overridden by model confidence
Candidate adoption is owned by the orchestrating Codex workflow and must cite persisted evaluation evidence rather than a permission prompt
Use multiple Agent roles only for context isolation, distinct authority or real parallel work
No framework, protocol, RAG or memory system is added without a measured requirement
Tests focus on contracts, policy, replay, recovery and external boundaries and should stay near 15-25 percent of implementation effort

Do not turn ordinary local operations, Codex-owned candidate adoption, screenshots or configured repository publishing into new approval gates; gates exist only for deterministic scene constraints, identity, irreversible writes and external side effects

Preserve the original product intent: prioritize practical AIGC-to-Unreal production capabilities and make the hand-built modern Agent control plane visible through real behavior, not framework accumulation
Every public metric identifies its dataset, denominator and inspectable evidence
Existing user work and historical source provenance must be preserved
All scene mutations are staged in a project-owned Data Layer, Level Instance or candidate level before publish; the source level is not overwritten in place
MCP is a thin adapter over the existing typed runtime and never owns a parallel state machine or arbitrary code-execution tool
Image-to-3D providers produce candidates only; no generated mesh enters a scene before license, Interchange, geometry, material, collision and budget validation
